query: Can you present the full inducing‑variable ELBO for the partitioned MoE GP (gating + H low‑rank LMC experts) with closed‑form KLs and analytic E_q[log p(Y|Z,F)] under factorized q(Z)?

response.query: Can you present the full inducing‑variable ELBO for the partitioned MoE GP (gating + H low‑rank LMC experts) with closed‑form KLs and analytic E_q[log p(Y|Z,F)] under factorized q(Z)?
response.answer: The full inducing-variable ELBO for partitioned MoE GP includes the log likelihood and KL divergence terms for both gating and low-rank LMC experts. It uses closed-form expressions for KLs and analytic E_q[log p(Y|Z,F)] under factorized q(Z). The ELBO optimizes the approximation of the posterior distribution.

results.title: Evidence Lower Bound: ELBO | Datumorphism | L Ma
results.content:
Title: Evidence Lower Bound: ELBO | Datumorphism | L Ma
# Evidence Lower Bound: ELBO. **wiki/machine-learning/bayesian/elbo.md** Current Note ID: The unique ID of this note. Given a probability distribution density $p(X)$ and a latent variable $Z$, we have the marginalization of the joint probability. $$ \int dZ p(X, Z) = p(X). In many models, we are interested in the log probability density $\log p(X)$ which can be decomposed using an auxiliary density of the latent variable $q(Z)$,. $$ \begin{align} \log p(X) =& \log \int dZ p(X, Z) \\ =& \log \int dZ p(X, Z) \frac{q(Z)}{q(Z)} \\ =& \log \int dZ q(Z) \frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z)} \\ =& \log \mathbb E\_q \left[ \frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z)} \right]. ](https://datumorphism.leima.is/cards/math/jensens-inequality/) Jensen's Inequality Jensen’s inequality shows that $$ f(\mathbb E(X)) \leq \mathbb E(f(X)) $$ for a concave function $f(\cdot)$. $$ \log \mathbb E\_q \left[ \frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z)} \right] \geq \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log\left(\frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z)}\right) \right], $$. $$ \begin{align} \log p(X) =& \log \mathbb E\_q \left[ \frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z)} \right] \\ \geq& \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log\left(\frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z)}\right) \right] \\ =& \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log p(X, Z)- \log q(Z) \right] \\ =& \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log p(X, Z) \right] - \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log q(Z) \right] . $$ H(q(Z)) = - \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log q(Z) \right] $$. $$ H(q(Z);p(X,Z)) = -\mathbb E\_q \left[ \log p(X, Z) \right] $$. $$ L = \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log p(X, Z) \right] - \mathbb E\_q \left[ \log q(Z) \right] = - H(q(Z);p(X,Z)) + H(q(Z)), $$. $$ \log p(X) \geq L. In a latent variable model, we might need to calculate the posterior $p(Z|X)$. To make sure we have a good approximation of the posterior, we find the KL divergence of $q(Z|\theta)$ and $p(Z|X)$. The ](https://datumorphism.leima.is/wiki/machine-learning/basics/kl-divergence/) KL Divergence Kullback–Leibler divergence indicates the differences between two distributions is. $$ \begin{align} D\_\text{KL}(q(Z|\theta)\parallel p(Z|X)) =& -\mathbb E\_q \log\frac{p(Z|X)}{q(Z|\theta)} \\ =& -\mathbb E\_q \log\frac{p(X, Z)/p(X)}{q(Z|\theta)} \\ =& -\mathbb E\_q \log\frac{p(X, Z)}{q(Z|\theta)} - \mathbb E\_q \log\frac{1}{p(X)} \\ =& - L + \log p(X). Since $D(q(Z|\theta)\parallel p(Z|X))\geq 0$, we have. $$ \log p(X) \geq L, $$. which also indicates that $L$ is the lower bound of $\log p(X)$. $$ L - \log p(X) = - D\_\text{KL}(q(Z|\theta)\parallel p(Z|X)) $$. `wiki/machine-learning/bayesian/elbo` Links to:. 'Evidence Lower Bound: ELBO', Datumorphism, 04 April. Available at: https://datumorphism.leima.is/wiki/machine-learning/bayesian/elbo/.
